_comment: Classify chain thresholds. One section per consuming class in jb/src/core/Services/Matching/Classify/, plus ImagePreProcessor (lives in Services/Matching/ but loads this file's ImagePreProcessor section directly — see ClassifyParameters.cs for the project-boundary reason). All edge/channel thresholds use the normalized [0,1] pixel scale unless noted.
_comment_subjectedgedetector: Calibrated 2026-08-05 (T-4990) against the 86 hand-verified intersection counts in test/datasets/SPACINI29/RAW IMAGES/dataset notes.md. Previous values (BgColorDiffThreshold 0.15, IntersectionFraction 0.20) scored 65/86 with 21 under-counts and zero over-counts; these score 84/86 with ZERO under-counts and 2 over-counts, and 70/70 on the two-edge images. IntersectionFraction is the dominant term: it is a fraction of the WHOLE strip area, and a model cut by the top edge touches it with head and shoulders — roughly 5-10% of a 384x30px band, never the 20% the old bar demanded. BgColorDiffThreshold 0.15 compounded it by reading light garments on a white sweep as background. MaxAnalysisSize was measured and does NOT matter here: 512 / 1024 / 2400 score identically at matched thresholds, so the T-4948 downscale interaction hypothesised on the ticket does not exist for this detector. StripDepthFraction is near-flat between 0.02 and 0.08 and gets worse at 0.10. MinRunLength must stay low: raising it to 8+ costs 4 points because a thin limb at an edge produces short runs.

SubjectDetector._comment_hardshadow: Fraction of the frame that must be stripped as thin texture-only line for hard-shadow evidence. Calibrated 2026-07-28 against SPACINI29 (n=86): the measured fraction runs min 0.0113 / median 0.0371 / p90 0.0702 / max 0.1243, so the previous 0.01 fired on 86/86 images and discriminated nothing while driving a bottom-trim on every centred image. 0.05 flags 23/86 (27%). This is a calibration choice on an unlabelled studio set, not ground truth; SubjectDetection.HardShadowStrippedFraction carries the raw measurement per image so it can be re-tuned against labelled data later.
SubjectDetector._comment_seeded: Toggle (b): a non-flat background is not one condition but two. B1 = a studio sweep (soft gradient, dust specks, sensor noise) fits the border-ring background plane closely; B2 = a real-life scene does not. RealLifeResidualThreshold is that discriminator, in Lab units of mean absolute plane-fit residual. B1 gets speckle tolerance; B2 gets HeroDetectionOnSteroids (higher analysis resolution, stricter blob filter). Toggle (a) needs no value here: it decides whether CLAHE runs at all, using ClaheClipLimit/ClaheTileSize above when it does.
